newsitem.title: PAKISTAN: Pakistani stocks close lower on rumours.
newsitem.headline: Pakistani stocks close lower on rumours.

text.p: Pakistani stocks closed lower on Monday on selling pressure amid rumours, which were denied by the central bank, that the government would freeze foreign currency accounts, dealers said.
The Karachi Stock Exchange (KSE) 100-share index closed 7.20 points, or 0.53 percent, lower at 1,355.58 amid 158 losers and 81 gainers.

The stocks fell before the State Bank of Pakistan denied the rumour, one dealer said. "The central bank's denial came after the rumour damaged the market." The market was likely to remain under pressure in the next few days.
"Investors lack confidence in Pakistan's economy and there is no investment coming in the stock market as the dollar offers better returns," another dealer said.
PTCL fell 0.50 to 33.65 rupees, Al-Ghazi Tractors 4.50 to 18.50, Packages 5.00 to 65, Milkpak 3.00 to 103, and Karachi Electric 0.75 to 20.50. HUBCO rose 0.05 to 30.65.
